title: The derived tensor product on the finite-Tor subcategories
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$, put
$A=A_{E,n}$, and let $X$ be a
finite-type
$k$-scheme. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ have
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$,
and let $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ be
bounded constructible.
Then:

1. **(i)** $K\otimes_A^LM$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,A)$;
1. **(ii)** if in addition $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ has finite Tor amplitude
in $[c,d]$, then $K\otimes_A^LM$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with
finite Tor amplitude in $[a+c,b+d]$.

proof.text: Install the proved closed symmetric monoidal, Grothendieck abelian and functorial flat-resolution structures on the constant-ring module sheaf category. Acyclic-tensor K-flatness implies categorical K-flatness: pass to the homotopy category and use the braiding to exchange the two tensor factors. The generic K-flat comparison DerivedCategory.QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft and the inverse of Q(f) identify the categorical tensor Q(K) tensor Q(M) with the given derivedTensor. For any derived object Z and ordered interval [a,b], compare the recorded HasProEtaleTorAmplitude with categorical torAmplitudeIn. In the forward direction choose a representative of Z and a K-flat resolution, using lem-pc-kflat-resolution; transport cohomology vanishing through the comparison and the single-complex comparison. In the reverse direction use the same comparison for every representative and resolution. All these comparisons are proved locally in the Lean proof.

Finite cohomological support of M supplies integer lower and upper bounds c and d, including when that support is empty. The categorical lower and upper tensor bounds give cohomology vanishing for K tensor M outside [a+c,b+d]. These existing source bounds use a bounded flat model of K and bounded representatives of M, so implement the flat-model and truncation argument of the source. Transport through the tensor comparison. The nonzero cohomology support is a subset of the finite integer interval, proving boundedness.

The cardinality of the finite base field gives characteristic p there and hence in its algebraic closure k. Since l and p are distinct primes, l is a unit in k. Map this unit into every residue field of X via the structure morphism and residue evaluation. Apply finiteTensor_constructible_cohomology to K and M, using the bounded-constructible component of finiteTorConstructible for K. This proves constructibility in every degree; together with boundedness this proves clause (i).

For clause (ii), let F be any module sheaf in degree zero. Tor amplitude of M makes M tensor F[0] cohomologically concentrated in [c,d]. Apply the same categorical lower and upper tensor bounds for K to this object and transport along tensor associativity. This proves categorical Tor amplitude of K tensor M in [a+c,b+d]. This uses the same bounded-flat-model tensor calculation as the source, encapsulated by the proved generic bounds, and avoids a second flat-model construction. Transport along the comparison to derivedTensor, apply the local amplitude equivalence in reverse, and use a+c <= b+d. Pair this amplitude with clause (i) and its own interval as a witness for finiteTorConstructible.
